_comment: THE BARE FHIR IG LAYER, staged as a top-level directory on the path who-iris, the WHO SMART Trust IG, the WHO SMART Immunizations IG and the WHO SMART Base IG are already on. Created 2026-09-22 on the owner's stack ruling: `core->fhir-harness-> smart-base->siblings{smart-l1, smart-dak, smart-ig}`, no smart-guidelines. It is bean `nsbb`'s 'base', now named: run the FHIR IG Publisher with NO pre-processing and NO post-processing and publish the result, which is how SMART Guidelines were built BEFORE the DAK phases were added -- a shape that demonstrably worked rather than one being invented. IT MUST STAY WHO-FREE. The package here may be referenced BY `authoring-who-smart-guidelines` and may never reference it; a violation fails nothing, the layer simply stops being usable by the non-WHO IG it exists for, which is why `ig-build-pipeline` states the refusal as a checkable list rather than as an intention. DECLARES ONLY `skills/`, because that is all that exists: a declared-but-absent directory is the `dh4f` defect, where every consumer scans nothing and reports a clean run over it.

title: FHIR IG Harness
description: The bare FHIR IG pipeline — SUSHI, the IG Publisher, Jekyll assembly and publication — with no WHO, DAK or SMART assumption. What a non-WHO implementation guide instantiates.

avatar.reads: a flame — the FHIR implementation-guide harness

_avatar_comment: A flame, for FHIR's own pun on its name. Moved here from cat-harness/schemas/avatars.ts, 2026-10-05 (bean sod4 #4): a layer declares its own mark.

directories.description: The gettext side of fhir-harness's own strings, one directory per target locale: the `processes/` templates of the BPMN diagrams this instance draws. A diagram's templates sit with the instance that draws it.

The validators fhir-harness's code provides, one folio-validator/v1 node each naming the graph typology and $schema family it checks. Validators are KG nodes, and the validator names the family. The registry joins each onto its kind.

The graph typologies fhir-harness owns, one folio-graph-typology/v1 node per file. There is no central registry of subgraph types: a harness declares its own in a typologies graph. The registry loads these on first use, across every instance, and refuses a kind two files declare.

L1 source content for the TEST side of a FHIR implementation guide -- FHIR test plans, the Gherkin test-language dialect, configuration for the Interoperability Test Bed -- with no WHO, DAK or SMART assumption: the R5 TestPlan resource's source (`hl7-2023-fhir-r5-testplan`, CC0), the Cucumber Gherkin reference (`cucumber-2024-gherkin-reference`, MIT) and the EC Interoperability Test Bed's README (`isaitb-2026-interoperability-test-bed-readme`, EUPL-1.2). They are here because nothing about them is WHO's, and no platform methodology cites them. The id is the conventional `library`, so this entry OVERRIDES the default rather than joining it.

Three packages. `content/fhir-ig-authoring` is authoring FHIR content: L3 artefacts from an L2 DAK, validation, terminology, publication, PCF consent and Questionnaire wireframes. `fhir-client` is SMART on FHIR app launch (`smart-launch`) and FHIR resource operations (`fhir-client-operations`) through the SMARTerFHIR library, authored here against a pinned upstream commit because that repository ships no skill files. `fhir-ig-base` is the IG pipeline. `ig-build-pipeline` states what the layer runs and the list of things it refuses to know about, including the deploy phase's assignment. `ig-render-jekyll` states the three render contracts -- JSON only, navigation derived from `sushi-config.yaml`'s own ordered `pages:` and `menu:` maps rather than authored, and the LHS rail with the IG theme captured. `ig-site-links` and `ig-site-theme` cover the rendered site's links and colour scheme, `ig-binary-artefacts` where the Publisher's binary outputs go, and `fhir-ig-create` starting a new IG. `ig-publisher-reduction` is the five-phase transition to an AST-only Publisher, each phase with a measured exit criterion. `ig-publisher-fork` is the brief for the AST work: a library ON TOP of the Publisher (`ast-export/` on `litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher@claude/ast-export`), with the Library/PlanDefinition/Measure edges supplied beside the publisher's own `DependencyAnalyser`, where upstream leaves them empty. Only page-fragment provenance needs `org.hl7.fhir.core`. `ig-ast-delta` is the consumer half: list, check (`compiledValidity` on the AST's inputs), diff and render deltas between ASTs, every page carrying the provisional mark P3 requires.

The Tool nodes of the FHIR IG pipeline, one directory per Tool, each naming the script it invokes: the FSH dependency cone and the FHIR package cache and mirror; the IG AST (export, list, validity, plan, incremental build, diff, render, refresh, JSON-LD, pages); the IG sites and their data, pages, menu, releases and terminology index; the JSON Schema and JSON-LD surfaces; Questionnaire checks; the binary audit; and the two `Library` strippers. None is DAK-shaped: the strippers, for example, serve any IG depending on `hl7.fhir.uv.cql`, which produces oversized `Library` resources.

The IG site pipeline's code and the Liquid templates it renders with: `stage-ig-sites.ts` stages each instance's IG as its own just-the-docs site, `build-ig-site.ts` turns an IG's `input/` and `sushi-config.yaml` into that site (navigation, colour scheme, the lifted `site.data.fhir` artefact variables, and the Publisher-generated pages `toc` and `artifacts`), `ig-site-data.ts` lifts the IG's `_data`, and `ig-ast.ts` lists, checks, diffs and renders IG ASTs. Templates sit under `templates/`, beside the writer that reads them (`liquid-templates`). The Tool nodes in `tools/` invoke these files.

The generic pipeline slots this instance fills, one folio-pipeline-plugin/v1 node per slot, naming PIPELINE_IMPLEMENTATIONS in pipeline/plugin-slots.ts. Today one: `site-publisher-ig`, the FHIR-IG site publisher that cat-harness-tools' stage-local.ts finds among the dependencies of the repository it publishes.

The one typed table of this instance's pipeline-slot implementations (`plugin-slots.ts`), which the nodes in pipeline-plugins/ name and the loader requires. It lies under harness-config's declared `*/pipeline/plugin-slots.ts` import glob, as folio-assistant-sci's table does.

The BPMN this layer OWNS, grouped by concern as the harness groups its own (`processes/<group>/`): in `content/`, the FHIR IG pipeline (`l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn`), its incremental build (`ig-incremental-build.bpmn`), the IG AST cache and delta review (`ig-ast-cache.bpmn`, `ig-ast-delta-review.bpmn`), the IG release, its owner's tag and its catch-up (`ig-release.bpmn`) and the Questionnaire wireframe review (`questionnaire-wireframe-review.bpmn`), beside the IG skills they bind.

directories.title: CI caches
directories.description: The caches this layer declares (cache-first CI, rule 6): one `cache/1.0.0` node per cache this layer's workflows and scripts hold. `fhir-ast.cache.json` is the IG AST branch store, whose component process is `processes/content/ig-ast-cache.bpmn`; `fhir-ig-tooling` and `fhir-cat-mount` are the Actions caches of the AST refresh. Staleness is computed by cat-harness-tools' `caches:viz`, never stated here.

Scenarios: the roles an actor takes on, in `roles.json`, the user stories told as them, in `stories.json`, the actors in `actors/`, and the capabilities in `capabilities/`: the FHIR modeller, IG Publisher service, publication manager and QC reviewer, and the SUSHI, IG Publisher and FHIR validator capability probes, beside the FHIR IG processes and skills they bind.

This layer's own documentation, composed THROUGH just-the-docs like the content core's docs directory, so its pages land in the platform's site under `/fhir-harness/` with the sidebar, search and layout. It holds the landing page (`index.md`), the FHIR pages (`fhir/`: the IG Publisher and FHIR content), their source (`source/`, declared as a `docs-source` by `docs.json` and rendered by the platform's one docs-page run), and `wireframes/`: the wireframe of each visualiser this layer declares (`ig-ast`), with its intent, checks and an `index.json` of the route keys it covers, which `check:wireframes` reads from every declared `docs` directory.

What auditing THIS instance produced, committed so a consumer can tell "never audited" from "audited clean" — a printed verdict cannot, which is why every QA verdict here is a sidecar. TWO kinds live here and the files declare which they are via $schema: kg-qa/v1, one per audited subject, in a tree mirroring the subject’s own path, and ONE kg-qa-manifest/v1 recording the auditor’s identity for all of them. The manifest moved here from skills/ on 2026-09-27: kg-audit.ts writes it unconditionally, so its old home created a skills/ directory holding no skills in every instance that has none. At declaration time that is 9 files across scenarios (1), skills (6), tools (2). No qa-results/v1 and no witnesses: this instance runs no document build and no witness-producing computation, and declaring kinds it does not hold would be an over-claim. dependents: reproduce, because a dependent audits its OWN graph — these verdicts are about this instance’s nodes, and inheriting them would attribute one instance’s findings to another. Declared WITH its files in one commit, per bean dh4f: a declared-but-absent directory makes a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run over it.

exempt.visualiser: No viewer by design. Each node is an outside package whose registry tarball and SPDX licence the node already links, so a viewer would only repeat the registry.

directories.title: Software libraries
directories.description: The outside libraries this layer's code imports or keeps vendored, one `software-library` node each. A dependency in `package.json` is a `software-library/1.0.0` node: the version and sha512 `bun.lock` pins, the registry tarball, the SPDX licence read from the installed package, the range, whether it is a dev dependency, and the files that import it (`usedBy`). A bundle kept under `scripts/assets/vendor/<name>/<version>/` (LHC-Forms, the NLM Form Builder, jQuery, ucum-lhc) is a `software-library/1.1.0` node marked `vendored`: name, version, tarball and sha512 from its `vendored.json`, and its licence from its own licence file (an NLM notice the SPDX list does not carry is a `LicenseRef-`). The imports inside a bundle are not this layer's, so they name no node. GENERATED, never hand-edited: `bun run cat libraries:derive` writes it and `libraries:check` fails on a stale node, an import no node names, a shim no node names, and a vendored file whose bytes are not the ones its `vendored.json` records. The kind is cat-harness's; this layer keeps its own nodes because it pins its own versions.

FHIR Harness's generated glossary (`glossary/generated/fhir-harness/`): candidate `folio-glossary/v1` schemes extracted from this layer's tools, skills, BPMN activities and schema fields by core's `glossary:page`. A scheme is keyed by (instance, scheme), and each layer holds its own glossary.

This layer's families are judged by its own commit. Written by `bun run cat node-kinds`, which only shrinks it; `--accept-unkinded` grows it deliberately.

_needs_comment: It sits directly on core. NOT on cat-harness: the harness layer is inherited through core rather than declared twice, in the same shape folio-assistant-core uses. Owner's ordering, 2026-09-20: bootstrap, cat-harness, f-a-core, then the layers above.
_canonicalUrl_comment: A placeholder base under this repository's own publication root, NOT a FHIR canonical: this layer publishes no FHIR artefacts, it publishes a Tool graph. It exists because a Tool node's I/O type IRIs are minted against it at load and Zod refuses a relative one. Stated rather than left blank so nobody reads it as a claim that fhir-harness is an IG.
_name_comment: THE NAME IS NOT AN INSTANTIATION CLAIM. `fhir-harness` is DECLARED here and is not instantiated: instantiation is a `<name>.config.json` at the REPOSITORY root (`harness-tiles`, bean `6n23`), and there is no `fhir-harness.config.json`. It also declares no `coverage.visualiser` on either directory, so by the tile rule it owes no tile and gets none — making it, measured 2026-09-23, the least harness-like thing in this repository that carries the word in its name. That is not a defect: this repository stages future layers as siblings, and `description` above says so ("What a non-WHO implementation guide instantiates") — a downstream IG instantiates it, this checkout does not. Written down because the name says otherwise to anyone who has not read the declaration, and `check:harness-claims` reports the pairing rather than leaving the next reader to re-derive it.

steps.reason: a BUILD step, not a check: it lists the IGs whose repositories carry an AST cache by asking each repository over the network; best effort (continue-on-error), its output only feeds the preview (bean `wnhh`)
a BUILD step, not a check: it clones each IG's recorded source and stages a Jekyll source; its logic is covered by stage-ig-sites.test.ts and build-ig-site.test.ts in `bun test` (bean `bamf`)
a DEPLOY step: it rewrites ids in ./_site, which only the staging job produces; dedupeIds is covered by build-ig-site.test.ts, and check:duplicate-ids judges the result (bean `bamf`)

scripts.reason: CI CANNOT OBTAIN ITS INPUT, and here it needs THREE checkouts rather than one. It compares the committed `chrome.json` against the `fhir.template` chain the IG's `ig.ini` names — `fhir.base.template` and `who.template.root`, which are separate repositories (`HL7/ig-template-base`, `WorldHealthOrganization/smart-ig-template`) that this checkout does not contain and a runner cannot fetch. The wall the retired `ingest:ig-menu:check` met, one layer worse: an IG's appearance is declared in no file the IG owns. Built so a skip CANNOT be mistaken for a pass — with no `--ig`/`--layer` it exits **2**, printing `could not determine`, rather than the 0 a silent skip would give. What IS gated, on every run and without the network, is the committed chrome's EFFECT: `smart-trust:pages:check` regenerates all 681 pages from it and compares them byte for byte, and `check:kind-validators` parses the file against `folio-ig-chrome/v1`. Run this one by hand after cloning the IG and its templates, or from `/prepare-merge`. Bean `ajx9`

_builtAtPublish_comment: Owner, 2026-10-14 (B1; schemas/built-at-publish.ts in cat-harness). This layer's JSON-LD @context is generated by `jsonld:contexts` (cat-harness-tools scripts/gen-instance-contexts.ts) from the prefixes and content-context terms its documents use, flattened with the prefix tables of every layer it needs. Those tables are read at the CHECKOUT's pins, not at pins this layer's commit names, so no commit of it can hold the file current: it is built at publish and never committed (bean folio-assistant-63q4).
